messages:
Ravi: Hey folks 1st day here. Trying to bootstrap dev env on Fedora 38 (work laptop). Installed Homebrew (Linuxbrew) in ~/.linuxbrew because the handbook suggested brew for some deps, cloned asdf into ~/.asdf, added `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh` into ~/.zshrc, but when I open VSCode integrated terminal the asdf shims aren't on PATH and `asdf` sometimes says 'command not found'. Any Fedora-specific quirks?

Lena: welcome! Fedora's default shells and GUI session handling can be quirky. VSCode spawns a non-login shell, so make sure to put PATH/shims exports in ~/.zprofile or ~/.profile (not only ~/.zshrc). For example: `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin:$PATH"` in ~/.profile and then `source ~/.zshrc` from ~/.zprofile if you need interactive config.

Chris: Also watch out for openssl versions. Fedora has openssl 3 by default; some old ruby/python builds expect openssl@1.1 libs. If asdf build fails with a crypto header missing error, install compat packages or point LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS to brew's openssl if you installed that: `export LDFLAGS='-L$HOME/.linuxbrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib'` etc. On Fedora you may prefer `dnf install compat-openssl11-devel` then no extra flags.

Ravi: That explains the ruby build failing with "unknown symbol EVP_..." error. I installed compat-openssl11-devel and reran `asdf install ruby 3.1.2` 1and it continued further. Thank you.

Lena: Nice. For NodeJS plugin on asdf, you might hit the gpg key import step. Run `~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring` and ensure gpg available in PATH. If gpg is the distro one, it usually works; if you installed gnupg via brew, make sure the brew bin is early in PATH.

Ravi: Ran the import script; got 'gpg: no writable keyring found' until I set GNUPGHOME to a writable dir under my home. So `export GNUPGHOME=$HOME/.gnupg-asdf` fixed that. Strange edgecase.

Chris: Good catch. Also if you use direnv, remember direnv can manage per-project LDFLAGS. Add `eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"` to your zsh startup so .envrc runs. We keep a snippet in our dotfiles: https://git.internal/redwood/dotfiles#linux-notes (check the 'linuxbrew & direnv' section).

Ravi: Quick ques: I'm trying to get 1Password CLI auth and SSH key working in the devcontainer. VSCode forwarding of SSH agent seems unreliable. Any recommended patterns?

Lena: We usually avoid trying to forward your host agent into containers. Instead we have a helper that runs in the container's entrypoint: `op signin --sh` + `op item get <ssh-key> --attributes privateKey | ssh-add -` and we store agent socket under /tmp/ssh-agent.sock mounted into the user workspace. That keeps the key in memory only inside the container. There's a script in dotfiles `scripts/container-op-ssh.sh` you can adapt.

Chris: If you want host forwarding, ensure `ssh-agent` on host is started and you set `forwardAgent: true` in the remote config; still it's racy. Container-side helper is simpler. Also watch 1Password session expiry: `eval "$(op signin --sh)"` creates OP_SESSION_* env vars; keep them in a direnv or run the sign-in command in your shell start.

Ravi: Thanks. Last hiccup: when I `asdf reshim` npm packages installed globally are not found until I re-open terminal. Is reshim supposed to be immediate?

Lena: reshim writes shims to ~/.asdf/shims; it should be immediate, but if your PATH cache or shell hash is stale, `hash -r` (zsh) clears it. Also ensure ~/.asdf/shims is first in PATH. If you installed a global npm binary and it's in the tool's bin dir, asdf should shim it; if not, check `asdf which <binary>` and `type -a <binary>`.

Chris: One more Fedora tip: GUI apps launched from Gnome session might not read ~/.profile. If you installed VSCode from the flatpak or distro package, try launching from terminal after sourcing your profile to validate.

Ravi: All good now: moved PATH exports to ~/.profile, installed compat-openssl11-devel, set GNUPGHOME for gpg, added direnv hook, and using the container helper for op/ssh. Appreciate the quick help :tada:
